node_text: The Bayes factor, which is the ratio of the conditional probability of an observation given A to the conditional probability of the observation given B, can be easier to measure than the individual conditional probabilities.
quote: Indeed frequently the ratio P (O1|A)/P (O1|B), called the Bayes factor, is easier to measure than either P (O1|A) or P (O1|B) separately; in messy, real-world scenarios the probability of the event O1 might be wrapped up with many uncertain factors that have nothing to do with either A or B.
